note.explanation: Chemistry has several branches so scientists can focus on different kinds of substances and questions. For example, analytical chemistry identifies and measures components in a sample, while environmental chemistry studies chemical effects in air, soil and water. Nuclear chemistry focuses on changes in atomic nuclei.
examples: Finding the components of a lunar sample: analytical chemistry.
Studying pollution caused by chemicals: environmental chemistry.
note.simple: Different chemistry branches are like different study areas: each one focuses on a particular kind of chemical question.
note.checkQuestion: Which branch deals with the separation, identification and measurement of components in a material?
note.title: What is Chemistry and why are there branches?
steps: Read what is being studied or measured.
Match it to the branch that focuses on that subject.
For a sample's components or concentrations, choose analytical chemistry.
note.answer: Chemistry studies substances, their properties, composition and structure, and changes in matter. Its branches focus on different aspects of this wide subject.

mcqs.stem: A scientist separates the components of a lunar sample and determines their concentrations. Which branch is most directly involved?
rationales: Correct: analytical chemistry involves separation, identification and determination of component concentrations.
Geochemistry studies the chemical composition of Earth and its sources and minerals.
Organic chemistry focuses on carbon compounds and their reactions.
Nuclear chemistry studies reactions and transformations in atomic nuclei.

mcqs.stem: Which branch studies chemical species and their effects in air, soil and water?
rationales: Correct: environmental chemistry studies chemical species in air, soil and water environments.
Polymer chemistry focuses on polymers and macromolecules.
Biochemistry studies chemical substances and vital processes in living organisms.
Astrochemistry studies molecules and ions in space and their interactions.

mcqs.stem: A study investigates transformations taking place in the nucleus of an atom. Which branch is it?
rationales: Correct: nuclear chemistry deals with reactions and transformations in atomic nuclei.
Physical chemistry investigates how substances behave at atomic and molecular levels, but the question specifically concerns nuclear transformations.
Geochemistry studies Earth's chemical composition, sources and minerals.
Medicinal chemistry focuses on designing and synthesizing medicines or drugs.

mcqs.stem: Which branch studies vital chemical processes in living organisms?
rationales: Correct: biochemistry studies chemical substances and vital processes in living organisms.
Inorganic chemistry studies elements and compounds containing little or no carbon.
Astrochemistry studies molecules and ions in space and interstellar space.
Analytical chemistry focuses on analyzing substances and their components.

mcqs.stem: The study of the structure, composition and reactions of carbon compounds (other than simple salts such as carbonates) belongs mainly to:
rationales: Correct: organic chemistry deals with carbon compounds other than specified simple salts.
Geochemistry studies the chemical composition of Earth and its sources and minerals.
Nuclear chemistry deals with reactions taking place in atomic nuclei.
Environmental chemistry studies chemical phenomena and species in the planet's air, soil and water.

mcqs.stem: A chemist designs and synthesizes a new drug intended to benefit people. Which branch is most directly involved?
rationales: Correct: medicinal chemistry includes designing and synthesizing medicines or drugs.
Polymer chemistry focuses on the properties, structure and synthesis of polymers.
Physical chemistry investigates how substances behave at atomic and molecular levels and helps predict reaction rates.
Analytical chemistry deals with separation, identification and determination of component concentrations.

written.text:
A lunar mission has recently brought samples from the Moon. The following experiments were then carried out on it. Point out the branch of chemistry these experiments are related to.

1. Determining its composition
2. Studying the physical properties of materials it contains
3. Carrying out chemical reactions with usual inorganic reagents
written.finalAnswer:
1. Analytical chemistry
2. Physical chemistry
3. Inorganic chemistry

rubric.why: The branch must match the analysis of sample composition.
rubric.description: Identifies analytical chemistry for determining composition.
rubric.how: Name analytical chemistry.

rubric.why: The branch must match the study of physical properties.
rubric.description: Identifies physical chemistry for studying physical properties.
rubric.how: Name physical chemistry.

rubric.why: The branch must match the use of inorganic reagents.
rubric.description: Identifies inorganic chemistry for the reactions with usual inorganic reagents.
rubric.how: Name inorganic chemistry.

modelAnswer: 1. Determining the sample's composition involves analysis of its components, so it is analytical chemistry.
2. Studying physical properties of materials is related to physical chemistry.
3. Reactions with usual inorganic reagents are related to inorganic chemistry.
Therefore, the branches are analytical chemistry, physical chemistry and inorganic chemistry, respectively.

written.text: Why is there a need to divide Chemistry into many branches? Give three reasons.
written.finalAnswer: Chemistry is a widely spread and complex subject, so it is divided into branches to focus on specific aspects, give scientists distinct areas of study, and help them achieve breakthroughs and advancements.

rubric.why: Recognizing the wide and complex nature of chemistry explains why it needs organization.
rubric.description: States that chemistry is widely spread or complex.
rubric.how: Mention that chemistry covers a very wide, complex subject.

rubric.why: Branches allow attention to particular aspects rather than the whole subject at once.
rubric.description: States that branches help focus on specific aspects.
rubric.how: Explain that each branch focuses on a particular aspect.

rubric.why: Branches provide distinct areas of study for scientists.
rubric.description: States that scientists get distinct areas of study.
rubric.how: Mention separate or specialized areas of study.

rubric.why: Specialized study supports progress in chemistry.
rubric.description: States that branches help achieve breakthroughs or advancements.
rubric.how: Mention breakthroughs or advancements.

modelAnswer: Chemistry is a widely spread and complex subject.
It is divided into branches so scientists can focus on specific aspects and have distinct areas of study.
This helps scientists achieve breakthroughs and advancements.

written.text: Reactions may take place due to electrons present outside the nucleus or they may take place inside the nucleus. Which branches of Chemistry cover these two types of reactions?
written.finalAnswer: Reactions involving electrons outside the nucleus are ordinary chemical reactions studied in the chemical branches of chemistry; reactions inside the nucleus are studied in nuclear chemistry.

rubric.why: The response must identify reactions involving outer electrons as chemical reactions.
rubric.description: Identifies ordinary chemical reactions involving electrons outside the nucleus.
rubric.how: State that these are chemical reactions involving electrons outside the nucleus.

rubric.why: The branch name for reactions inside the nucleus is essential.
rubric.description: Identifies nuclear chemistry for reactions inside the nucleus.
rubric.how: Name nuclear chemistry.

modelAnswer: Reactions involving electrons outside the nucleus are ordinary chemical reactions.
Reactions taking place inside the nucleus are studied in nuclear chemistry.

written.text: What types of problems are solved in analytical chemistry?
written.finalAnswer: Analytical chemistry solves problems involving the separation, identification and determination of the concentration of components present in material things.

rubric.why: These are central analytical tasks stated in the textbook.
rubric.description: Mentions separation and identification of components.
rubric.how: State that analytical chemistry separates and identifies components.

rubric.why: Determining component concentrations is another key task of analytical chemistry.
rubric.description: Mentions determining the concentration of components.
rubric.how: State that it determines component concentrations.

modelAnswer: Analytical chemistry deals with the analysis of different substances.
It solves problems involving separation, identification and determination of the concentration of components present in material things.

written.text: Most of the molecules we study in biochemistry are organic in nature. Where does the difference exist in organic and biochemistry branches of Chemistry?
written.finalAnswer: Organic chemistry studies the structure, formation, properties, composition and reactions of carbon compounds. Biochemistry studies chemical substances and vital processes in living organisms, including the structure and function of biological molecules.

rubric.why: The key distinction is the subject matter of organic chemistry.
rubric.description: Explains that organic chemistry studies carbon compounds and their properties or reactions.
rubric.how: Describe organic chemistry as the study of carbon compounds, including their structure or reactions.

rubric.why: Biochemistry is identified by its focus on living organisms and their processes.
rubric.description: Explains that biochemistry studies chemical substances or processes in living organisms.
rubric.how: Mention living organisms or vital processes.

rubric.why: Biochemistry also considers the structure and function of biological molecules.
rubric.description: Adds that biochemistry studies biological molecules and their structure or function.
rubric.how: Give an example such as proteins, carbohydrates, lipids or nucleic acids, or mention molecular structure/function.

modelAnswer: Organic chemistry deals with carbon compounds, including their structure, formation, properties, composition and reactions.
Biochemistry studies chemical substances and vital processes occurring in living organisms.
It also gives insights into the structure and function of molecules such as proteins, carbohydrates, lipids and nucleic acids.
Thus, organic chemistry focuses on carbon compounds, while biochemistry focuses on chemical processes and molecules in living organisms.

written.text:
Mention the name of the branch of Chemistry in which you will study each of the following topics.

(a) Rate of a reaction
(b) Digestion of food in human body
(c) Properties of plasma
(d) Ecosystem
(e) Reactions taking place during fireworks
(f) Measurement of the absorption of wavelength with the help of ultraviolet spectrometer
written.finalAnswer:
(a) Physical chemistry
(b) Biochemistry
(c) Physical chemistry
(d) Environmental chemistry
(e) Inorganic chemistry
(f) Analytical chemistry

rubric.why: Reaction rates and physical behaviour are studied through physical chemistry.
rubric.description: Correctly assigns physical chemistry to reaction rate and properties of plasma.
rubric.how: Give physical chemistry for (a) and (c).

rubric.why: Digestion is a chemical process in a living organism.
rubric.description: Correctly assigns biochemistry to digestion.
rubric.how: Give biochemistry for (b).

rubric.why: An ecosystem is an environmental subject.
rubric.description: Correctly assigns environmental chemistry to ecosystem.
rubric.how: Give environmental chemistry for (d).

rubric.why: Fireworks commonly involve chemical reactions studied as inorganic chemistry in this classification.
rubric.description: Correctly assigns inorganic chemistry to fireworks reactions.
rubric.how: Give inorganic chemistry for (e).

rubric.why: Instrumental measurement of absorption is an analysis of a substance.
rubric.description: Correctly assigns analytical chemistry to wavelength absorption measurement.
rubric.how: Give analytical chemistry for (f).

modelAnswer: (a) Rate of a reaction — Physical chemistry
(b) Digestion of food in human body — Biochemistry
(c) Properties of plasma — Physical chemistry
(d) Ecosystem — Environmental chemistry
(e) Reactions taking place during fireworks — Inorganic chemistry
(f) Measurement of absorption with an ultraviolet spectrometer — Analytical chemistry

written.text: Differentiate between the areas which are studied under inorganic and organic chemistry.
written.finalAnswer: Inorganic chemistry studies the synthesis, composition, properties and structure of elements and compounds that contain little or no carbon. Organic chemistry studies carbon compounds (hydrocarbons and their derivatives), other than simple salts such as carbonates, bicarbonates, oxides and carbides, including their structure, formation, properties, composition and reactions.

rubric.why: The carbon content is the basic distinction given for inorganic substances.
rubric.description: Describes inorganic chemistry as studying substances with little or no carbon.
rubric.how: State that inorganic chemistry concerns elements and compounds with little or no carbon.

rubric.why: The answer should explain the areas studied in inorganic chemistry.
rubric.description: Mentions synthesis, composition, properties or structure of inorganic substances.
rubric.how: Give at least one of the textbook's inorganic areas of study.

rubric.why: Carbon compounds define the main area of organic chemistry.
rubric.description: Describes organic chemistry as the study of carbon compounds.
rubric.how: State that organic chemistry deals with carbon compounds or hydrocarbons and derivatives.

rubric.why: Organic chemistry also studies what these compounds are like and how they change.
rubric.description: Mentions organic compounds' structure, properties, composition or reactions and the simple-salt exception.
rubric.how: Add a studied feature or name the exception for simple carbon salts.

modelAnswer: Inorganic chemistry studies the synthesis, composition, properties and structure of elements and compounds that contain little or no carbon.
Organic chemistry deals with carbon compounds (hydrocarbons and their derivatives), except simple salts such as carbonates, bicarbonates, oxides and carbides.
It studies the structure, formation, properties, composition and reactions of carbon-containing compounds.

examTips: Branch-identification questions may describe an experiment or topic; match its focus to the branch's definition.
For a comparison question, define both branches and state the key difference in their subject matter.

For a question asking why chemistry is divided into branches, give three separate reasons: the subject is complex, branches focus on specific aspects, and specialization helps scientists make breakthroughs and advancements.
For the lunar-sample activity, link composition analysis to analytical chemistry, physical properties to physical chemistry, and inorganic reagents to inorganic chemistry.

explain.title: What chemistry studies
explain.body: Chemistry is the branch of science which deals with the properties, composition and the structure of substances. It also deals with the physical and chemical changes in matter and the laws or principles which govern these changes.

explain.title: Why chemistry has branches
explain.body: Chemistry is a widely spread, complex subject. Its branches give scientists distinct areas to focus on, making it possible to study specific aspects and achieve breakthroughs and advancements.

explain.title: Physical and analytical chemistry
explain.body: Physical chemistry investigates how substances behave at atomic and molecular levels. Analytical chemistry deals with the analysis of substances through separation, identification and determination of component concentrations.

explain.title: Organic, inorganic and nuclear chemistry
explain.body: Organic chemistry deals with carbon compounds other than simple salts such as carbonates, bicarbonates, oxides and carbides. Inorganic chemistry studies elements and compounds that contain little or no carbon. Nuclear chemistry deals with reactions taking place in an atom's nucleus.

explain.title: Chemistry in living things, the environment and space
explain.body: Biochemistry studies chemical substances and vital processes in living organisms. Environmental chemistry studies chemical phenomena and species in air, soil and water. Astrochemistry studies molecules and ions in space and interstellar space.

mistakes: Mixing up analytical chemistry (analyzing components) with a branch that studies what substances do or how they behave.
Calling every study of a carbon-containing molecule biochemistry: organic chemistry studies carbon compounds, while biochemistry focuses on living organisms and their chemical processes.
Confusing inorganic chemistry with nuclear chemistry: inorganic chemistry concerns elements and compounds with little or no carbon; nuclear chemistry concerns reactions in atomic nuclei.
Giving only one reason when asked for three reasons chemistry is divided into branches.
Writing a branch name without linking it to the topic in a branch-identification question.
